meta.purpose: Master priority hierarchy. When two things compete for the same hour, the higher priority wins. No exceptions.
meta.governingRule: Professional development must complement academic learning, never interfere with examination preparation. During the 12 weeks before an exam window, professional skills pause except communication practice, which continues because it is cheap and compounds.

priorities.name: CMA Intermediate Group I — December 2026
priorities.why: The immediate gate. Everything else is subordinate until this is cleared.
priorities.successMeasure: All four papers attempted with a mock average at or above 60% and no paper below 50%.
nonNegotiable: Minimum 3 hours of active study on a working day
One full-length paper every week from September

priorities.name: CMA Intermediate Group II — June 2027
priorities.why: Completing both groups unlocks Final and the professional tier.
priorities.successMeasure: Mock average ≥ 60% across all four papers before the exam form deadline.
nonNegotiable: Start Group II within four weeks of the December result
Do not start Final before Group II mocks reach 60%

priorities.name: CMA Final — after Intermediate and eligibility
priorities.why: The professional qualification itself. Cannot start before both Intermediate groups are cleared and the practical training requirements are met.
priorities.successMeasure: Registration completed only after eligibility is confirmed with ICMAI.

gates.gate: Practical training requirement confirmed with ICMAI

nonNegotiable: Do not buy Final study material before eligibility is confirmed
Do not let Final planning distract from Group II

priorities.name: Professional Accounting and Finance Skills
priorities.why: The practical layer that converts exam knowledge into employability — but it sits below the exams.
priorities.successMeasure: At least five documented portfolio artefacts with full documentation.

gates.gate: One project presented aloud and recorded

nonNegotiable: Skills practice never displaces a scheduled mock
Every skill hour must produce an artefact

priorities.name: AI, Data Analytics, Automation and Technology
priorities.why: The differentiator over the next five years, pursued in short cycles between exam phases.
priorities.successMeasure: One working automation with a measured evaluation and a governance note.
nonNegotiable: Build the manual process before automating it
Never use real or client data in a model

priorities.name: Career Development, Certifications and Portfolio
priorities.why: Crystallises the rest into opportunity, but only once there is something real to show.
priorities.successMeasure: A resume with five quantified achievements and a portfolio that a stranger can navigate.
nonNegotiable: No certification purchased without checking whether a target role requires it
No claim on a resume that cannot be evidenced

examWindows.note: Confirm dates from the ICMAI timetable when published.

timeBudget.note: The split shifts by phase. In the 12 weeks before an exam window, skills and technology hours move to mocks and revision.

escalationTriggers.trigger: Mock average below 50% for two consecutive weeks
escalationTriggers.action: Suspend all priority 4–6 activity for 14 days and rebuild fundamentals.

escalationTriggers.trigger: More than 20% of planned study hours missed for two weeks
escalationTriggers.action: Reduce the plan, not the standards — cut an activity rather than pretending to do everything.

escalationTriggers.trigger: Same error type repeated three times
escalationTriggers.action: Write the rule in the mistake log and drill it before any new topic.

escalationTriggers.trigger: No artefact produced in four weeks of skills work
escalationTriggers.action: Stop the course and finish one project.
